The gql description gave the example `gender == 1`, which Gramps Web
rejects with 422 "Expected end of text, found '='". An agent that
follows it gets a parse error on its first filter.

The description now shows `=` for equality and lists the operators.
It also says that text goes in double quotes, since unquoted non-ASCII
text fails to parse with the same misleading error. And it says that
types are numbers: `type = "Birth"` matches nothing, while
`type.value = 12` finds births. It names the common event types.

Two integration tests hold Gramps Web to this syntax: `=` with quoted
text finds the record while `==` fails, and an event type matches by
number but not by name. The tool catalog row and the changelog Keep the image attestations out of GHCR

GHCR has no OCI referrers API, so actions/attest stored each image's
attestation under a tag named after the image digest, sha256-<digest>.
Every push to main added one more of these tags to the package page,
and none went away when latest moved on.

The image job no longer pushes the attestation to the registry. GitHub
still keeps it, and `gh attestation verify oci://...` reads it from
there, so the check in the README and SECURITY.md works as before. The
README, the developer guide and the changelog no longer mention a copy
in Show what to ask the agent

The README listed the tools by what they do, which tells a new user
little about what to type into the chat.

A "What to ask" section after the features now gives twelve requests
in plain words, from a person's great-grandparents and how two people
are related to transcribing a scan, adding a family from a sentence
and undoing the last edit. Each names the tools a typical run uses and
what comes back. The notes below say which requests work in read-only
mode, which need media access or an upload folder, that deletes and
undos wait for the user's confirmation, and which guided prompts cover
the same ground. The tool names are real ones, so the documentation
test keeps them in step with the server.

The GitHub Pages features section ends with six of the requests and a
link to the full table, styled for both themes, and the changelog
follows.","tree":{"sha":"d72a2212afddadffbfc125c61abc1bde01a1ebaf","url":"https://api.github.com/repos/Scormave/gramps-web-mcp/git/trees/d72a2212afddadffbfc125c61abc1bde01a1ebaf"},"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/Scormave/gramps-web-mcp/git/commits/d4dd853b9916497f31b74277e7d62f64ce58b38f","comment_count":0,"verification":{"verified":false,"reason":"unsigned","signature":null,"payload":null,"verified_at":null}},"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/Scormave/gramps-web-mcp/commits/d4dd853b9916497f31b74277e7d62f64ce58b38f","html_url":"https://github.com/Scormave/gramps-web-mcp/commit/d4dd853b9916497f31b74277e7d62f64ce58b38f","comments_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/Scormave/gramps-web-mcp/commits/d4dd853b9916497f31b74277e7d62f64ce58b38f/comments","author":{"login":"Scormave","id":5045197,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjUwNDUxOTc=","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/5045197?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave","html_url":"https://github.com/Scormave","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"committer":{"login":"Scormave","id":5045197,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjUwNDUxOTc=","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/5045197?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave","html_url":"https://github.com/Scormave","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scor Add install buttons for VS Code and Cursor

Connecting VS Code or Cursor meant copying the Docker stdio entry into
the editor's MCP settings by hand.

The README, right below its introduction, and the GitHub Pages quick
start now carry buttons for VS Code, VS Code Insiders and Cursor that
add this entry with one click; the README's Docker stdio section
explains them and points up to them. The VS Code links go through the
insiders.vscode.dev redirect, which opens the editor's install page.
They declare four prompts, so VS Code asks for the Gramps Web address,
user name, password and tree ID when the server starts for the first
time and keeps the password in its secret storage. Cursor's link
carries the same command with the placeholders shown in the README, to
replace before the first start.

The HTTP setup gets no button: the address is the user's own server,
and VS Code does not fill prompts into a URL reliably. The release
binary gets none either, as it needs a local path.

The site's buttons get light-theme colours, and the changelog Attest the release files and the image

SHA256SUMS only tells a download from a broken one: whoever could
replace a release file could replace the checksums with it. Nothing
tied the bundles, the archives or the image to this repository's
workflows.

Both workflows now create build provenance attestations with
actions/attest: a record of the repository, workflow and commit that
built each file, signed through Sigstore and stored by GitHub. The
release workflow attests the bundles, the archives and SHA256SUMS in one
attestation before it attaches them, so a release never carries files
without one. The image workflow attests the multi-platform index it
pushes by digest, which covers every tag of that push, and puts a copy
in GHCR next to the image. Storage records exist only for organization
repositories, so the image step skips them.

The publishing jobs gain id-token and attestations write permissions;
the image job's comment on who may request an OIDC token follows.

`gh attestation verify <file> --repo Scormave/gramps-web-mcp`, or
oci://ghcr.io/scormave/gramps-web-mcp:<tag> for an image, checks a
download. The README shows it for the image, the archives and the
bundles, and notes that gh asks Docker Desktop for registry
credentials and hangs while Docker Desktop is not running. SECURITY.md
gains a section on verifying downloads; the release checklist verifies
an archive and the image after each release and says what to re-run
when an attestation step fails; the MCPB README, developer guide,
architecture notes and changelog Attach the server binary to each release

The only ready-made way to run the server without Docker was the MCPB
bundle, and only Claude Desktop installs it. Cursor, VS Code, Codex,
Claude Code and other clients on a machine without Docker had to build
from source with the .NET SDK.

The pack script now also packs the bundle's self-contained binary with
LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt into gramps-web-mcp-<rid>.tar.gz
(.zip for win-x64, with zip or 7-Zip, since Windows runners have no
zip). The files sit at the archive's root, so a newer release unpacks
over the old one, and the name carries no version, so
releases/latest/download/<name> always fetches the newest. macOS tar
runs with COPYFILE_DISABLE so it adds no ._ entries.

The release workflow uploads the archives with the bundles, writes
SHA256SUMS and attaches all of them to the release, failing on a
missing file. Since neither packs only MCPB bundles any more,
mcpb-release.yml becomes release-assets.yml ("Release assets"), its
build-mcpb job becomes build, and scripts/pack-mcpb.sh becomes
scripts/pack-release.sh.

smoke-test.py gains an archive mode: it checks that the archive holds
only the three files, with the binary executable, and starts the
binary with only the Gramps settings in its environment, so stdio must
be the default. It runs on the linux-x64 and osx-arm64 legs after the
bundle check.

The README's "Other MCP clients" adds the release binary as a third
way: the archives, download commands for macOS, Linux and Windows, the
client entry, updating, the macOS quarantine mark after a browser
download, and the glibc and ICU requirement on Linux. The MCPB README,
release checklist, developer guide, architecture notes, license key
reminder, changelog, the site's client panel and ReleaseVersionTests
follow.","tree":{"sha":"609f10980fe38ea434e6d888f1fe9bb33f8e70c6","url":"https://api.github.com/repos/Scormave/gramps-web-mcp/git/trees/609f10980fe38ea434e6d888f1fe9bb33f8e70c6"},"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/Scormave/gramps-web-mcp/git/commits/939acd393ea42e512434f36660f56be9e9a3f058","comment_count":0,"verification":{"verified":false,"reason":"unsigned","signature":null,"payload":null,"verified_at":null}},"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/Scormave/gramps-web-mcp/commits/939acd393ea42e512434f36660f56be9e9a3f058","html_url":"https://github.com/Scormave/gramps-web-mcp/commit/939acd393ea42e512434f36660f56be9e9a3f058","comments_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/Scormave/gramps-web-mcp/commits/939acd393ea42e512434f36660f56be9e9a3f058/comments","author":{"login":"Scormave","id":5045197,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjUwNDUxOTc=","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/5045197?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave","html_url":"https://github.com/Scormave","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"committer":{"login":"Scormave","id":5045197,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjUwNDUxOTc=","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/5045197?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scormave","html_url":"https://github.com/Scormave","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/Scorm Smoke-test the image and the bundles before publishing

The release workflows published whatever compiled: the 2.5.0 bundle
shipped with a manifest default (${HOME}/Downloads) that the server
rejected at startup, and nothing ran the packed binary before release.

scripts/smoke-test.py (Python 3.9+, standard library only) starts the
built server against a stand-in for Gramps Web on 127.0.0.1 and runs
MCP over it: initialize with the expected version, the tool, prompt
and resource lists (core tools present; no editing tools in read-only
mode), and get_reference metadata, which reads the stand-in's tree.

- image mode: the image must not run as root; over HTTP it checks
  /health, 401 without or with a wrong API key, 403 for a foreign
  Origin, X-Api-Key, MCP, and the HEALTHCHECK command inside the
  container; then the same MCP checks over stdio. Secrets stay off
  the docker command line.
- mcpb mode: unpacks the bundle, checks the manifest version and that
  every ${user_config.X} is declared, then starts the binary from the
  manifest with the defaults passed literally, as Claude Desktop
  does, and checks that it exits when stdin closes.

On failure the log shows the checks that passed, the one that failed,
the server's log and the requests the stand-in received.

docker.yml builds and loads the amd64 image and smoke-tests it before
it logs in and pushes; the multi-platform build reuses its layers.
mcpb-release.yml smoke-tests the linux-x64 and osx-arm64 bundles,
which their runners can start, and publish-release now runs only on
v* tags, so a manual dispatch on a branch is a dry run.

RELEASING.md, the developer guide and the changelog describe the
smoke test and how to run it Scan the published images with Trivy every week

Published images are never rebuilt, so a vulnerability fixed in Ubuntu
or .NET after a release stays in its image, and ci.yml sees only NuGet
packages. image-scan.yml now scans the image of the latest GitHub
Release and :latest on GHCR every Monday and on demand:

Check the release tag against the committed version

A tag pushed before the release commit, or a release commit that misses
a step of RELEASING.md, used to publish an image, MCPB bundles and a
registry entry under the wrong version. Two checks now stop it:

- scripts/check-release-version.sh <tag> passes only when the tag is
  v<x.y.z>, the csproj declares <Version>x.y.z</Version> and
  CHANGELOG.md has a dated "## [x.y.z]" section. docker.yml (test job),
  the Gitea docker.yml and a new release-version job that the MCPB
  matrix needs run it on v* tags before anything is built;
- ReleaseVersionTests keeps server.json (version and OCI image tag), the
  newest changelog section (dated, with entries), the compare link of
  every version and the pack-mcpb.sh examples on the csproj version.

RELEASING.md runs the script before git tag; the developer guide and
